adversarial_direction: Steelman the case AGAINST the DIR-001 (housing-finance, borrowing-funded) beneficiary tier: argue funding-cost transmission is slower or smaller than modeled, so the NIM-expansion mechanism disappoints relative to what is already priced.
bear_case_steelman: System liquidity was already loose before the cut (M0_6_1 contrary view), so incremental CP/NCD repricing may lag the clean 2-quarter roll assumed in M0_6_3 — HFCs could see funding costs fall more slowly than the 50 bps headline implies, while NIFTY Financial Services already re-rated to the top third of its 5-year forward P/E band (M0_6_2 block 3) on day one. If the funding-cost transmission comes in materially slower than modelled, Q2 FY27 results could show only a partial NIM benefit against a valuation base that has already moved — a 'buy the rumor, mediocre on the print' outcome the thesis does not currently price.
world_change_attack: The three WC-001/002/003 magnitudes hold up against their stated baselines (prior MPC level, prior-day close, prior-day weighted average) — all same-day, same-source, non-cherry-picked windows. No attack survives here.
variant_perception_attack: The +15-20 bps NIM / +4-6% EPS departure (M0_6_3) is a real, mechanism-specific number, not a restatement of the +1% uniform consensus drift (M0_6_2 block 2) — the funding-mix asymmetry is a genuine, differentiated claim. Weakness: `sell_side_gap_evidence` describes a search over 'published-summary aggregators' on the SAME day as the event (2026-06-10) — a same-day search is a weak test of a sell-side coverage gap; the street has had less than 24 hours to publish a differentiated read. This should be re-checked closer to the M0_6_5 trigger window, not treated as settled.
mispricing_reason_attack: The three verifiable facts (uniform day-one sub-index moves; undifferentiated 48h estimate revisions; the off-cycle date missing from the standard model-update calendar) are independent — they test three different things (price action, analyst output, analyst calendar) rather than one fact restated three ways. They hold up.
convergence_trigger_attack: The 4-step causal_mechanism rests on Q2 FY27 results (2026-10-15 to 2026-11-15) being the moment NIM expansion becomes visible — a mandatory, scheduled disclosure (SEBI LODR Reg 33), not a discretionary event. No named-actor step is hand-wavy. Residual risk (not a break, a timing note): if funding costs reprice faster than the 1-2 quarter assumption, some of the NIM benefit could already show in Q1 FY27 commentary before the named trigger window, pulling convergence earlier than modelled — worth monitoring, not a disqualifying flaw.

falsification_attack.rationale: Threshold: 3-month AAA HFC CP yield must decline >=25 bps from the 2026-06-09 baseline by 2026-08-15 (about 9 weeks after the cut) or the thesis is dead. Against a 50 bps repo cut and a 42 bps same-day call-money repricing (WC-003), a 25 bps CP move within 9 weeks is a realistic, readily observable bar — meaningfully short of the full 50 bps transmission, not set so far away it could never fire. The by-date (2026-08-15) sits comfortably inside the M0_4 horizon (expiry ~Oct-Nov 2026), leaving a real window to observe a breach before the thesis is judged on results anyway. This is a genuine, reachable test, not a fireproof one.

base_rate_check: A 25-45 bps funding-cost pass-through within one to two quarters of a 50 bps policy cut is within the historical range for India's money-market transmission (per M0_6_1's own contrary-view citation of a +35 bps CP-repo spread forecast vs a +15 bps historical spread) — the implied magnitude is not an outlier requiring exceptional evidence; it sits inside a plausible, previously-observed band.
